subject: Food Science
title: Acrylamide in Food
description: Learn Acrylamide in Food in one minute.

hook.text: In 2002, Swedish scientists found acrylamide—a potential carcinogen—in french fries, chips, and toast.

buildup.text: Acrylamide forms during the Maillard reaction when asparagine reacts with reducing sugars above 120°C.

discovery.text: Darker-roasted foods contain more acrylamide. Golden fries have less than dark brown ones.

twist.text: The discovery caused global alarm, but the actual cancer risk from dietary acrylamide remains debated among scientists.

climax.text: The EU now regulates benchmark levels. 'Go for gold, not brown' became official advice for home cooks.

punchline.text: Browning makes flavor—but push too far and chemistry bites back.

quiz.question: When does acrylamide form in food?
options: When asparagine and sugars react above 120°C during Maillard browning
